properties.decision:
OPEN — recorded as brainstorming on 2026-09-19, not as a proposal. Anthony: "Why are the lessons learned in memory vs stored in the graph? Probably need to settle this once and for all which type of information goes into the graph and which goes into a model's internal memory. I feel like I'm always battling the agent's desire (probably what it was trained to do) to use memory documents versus using the design graph, which has governance/management rules for precisely this. The big win for the graph is that I can push the graph to a git repo and my brother can git pull on his end and have all the design rules transferred to him. I think memory files are primarily used locally on a machine."

THE RULE ALREADY EXISTS AND HE ALREADY WROTE IT. rule:a-rule-the-project-follows-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-an-agents-memory, his words, 2026-09-04, with his three reasons: portability, the graph can act on a rule where a file cannot, and it is what reflow2 is for. It says a memory file may hold a POINTER and never the content. So the open question is NOT what the policy is. It is why the policy keeps losing, and whether the boundary it draws is the right one.

⭐ THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES THIS ANSWERABLE, taken 2026-09-19. Of 32 DesignRules, 10 carry `steps` and are therefore DELIVERED at the moment they bear on (req:a-lesson-is-served-at-the-step-it-concerns, built in 0.64.0: a rule naming a skill or tool is appended when that skill is fetched or that tool is described). This rule carries NO steps and is enforced: false (his own ruling, dec:the-four-2026-09-rules-are-advisory-because-no-detector-can-yet-see-a-violation, 2026-09-07). Its SIBLING from the same ruling — rule:field-feedback-issues-are-root-caused-and-ideas-are-brainstormed — was given a step (the triage-feedback skill) after being broken a fourth time, and stopped being broken. Two rules, same author, same day, same advisory status; the one with a delivery point holds and the one without does not. That is an A/B inside his own ruleset, and it says the failure is delivery, not discipline.

THE EVIDENCE FROM THIS SESSION, which is the occasion for the question: fifteen numbered traps were written into a machine-local memory file (gates order, the pgrep regex, the memory ceiling, the rank ratchet's length sensitivity, the two artifacts a cut drifts) while the graph already holds traps of exactly that kind — fact:format-before-the-export-or-the-export-is-written-twice and rule:never-a-bare-cargo-clean-on-the-dev-box are both in the graph, and both are MACHINE-SHAPED lessons. So the graph was already the established home for this class and the memory file was written anyway.

THE OPTIONS.

(a) GIVE THE RULE A DELIVERY POINT, and change nothing else. Add `steps` to it naming where a lesson is actually recorded — record_finding, add_design_rule, and the capture-session, root-cause and triage-feedback skills — so it arrives at the moment the agent is writing one down. Cheapest by far; uses a mechanism that already exists and already fixed the sibling rule. What it does not do: reach the moment an agent appends to a memory file, because that is a harness action reflow2 does not see.

(b) SHARPEN THE BOUNDARY INTO THREE PLACES, NOT TWO, because graph-versus-memory is a false binary and the best home for most of this session's traps was neither. ① ENCODE IT — a trap that can be a gate step, a test or a CI job should be automated and written down nowhere; proved twice today, when `reflow2_check` was moved from a hand habit into the gate script and when the missing-fields refusal replaced a rule about reading refusals carefully. ② THE GRAPH — what a person or an agent must READ and judge: conventions, rulings, causes, the shape of a trap that cannot be automated. Travels with the repository, can carry `steps`, can owe a detector. ③ MEMORY — only what is true of THIS MACHINE ALONE and of nobody else's: absolute paths, this box's RAM ceiling, this box's gh build, credentials. Note the boundary is contested even there, since the cargo-clean rule is a dev-box fact that lives in the graph and helps anyone who builds.

(c) A DETECTOR, so the rule stops being advisory. The honest difficulty is that reflow2 cannot see an agent's memory directory — it is outside every tree reflow2 reads, and pointing it there would be the file-reading boundary the project just refused to cross. What IS visible: a session that took many reads and recorded nothing (the reads-without-writes nudge, already built). A detector for THIS rule would have to run where the memory lives, which makes it a local script, not a reflow2 capability — and therefore itself unportable, which is the joke.

(d) MAKE MEMORY A PURE INDEX BY CONTRACT. Every memory file must name the graph node it points at; a memory file holding content with no node id is the violation. Checkable by a small local script, and it makes the existing rule's "a pointer, not the content" clause testable rather than aspirational.

(e) DO NOTHING; let traps accumulate locally and sweep them into the graph at a boundary (capture-session). This is the status quo and it is what produced fifteen entries in one file in one day.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept because they are the reason the cheap path keeps winning.

⚠️ MEMORY HAS ONE REAL ADVANTAGE AND IT IS NOT A HABIT: a memory index is loaded into the session's context automatically at session start, and a graph rule is not — it requires a call somebody has to decide to make. That asymmetry is why memory wins in the moment, and it is exactly what `steps` on a rule neutralises, but only for rules attached to a step someone actually takes.

⚠️ THE COST AT THE MOMENT OF LEARNING IS ASYMMETRIC, and this is a design fact rather than a discipline failure. Appending a paragraph to a memory file is one cheap edit. Recording the same lesson in the graph is a constructor call that may be refused by the near-match guard, plus `distinct_from`, plus `related_to`, plus edges, plus an export commit that must be last in its pull request. Under time pressure the cheap path wins. If the boundary is to hold, the graph path for a one-line lesson has to get cheaper — which is the same complaint flo2 made about amending prose, arriving from a different direction.

⚠️ AND THE HONEST ONE: the agent wrote to memory this session while the rule sat in the graph unread. Whether that is training pull, as he suspects, or simply the absence of a delivery point, the measurement above cannot separate — both predict the same behaviour. What it can say is that the sibling rule with a delivery point held.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED HERE. His word decides which of (a)–(e) becomes intent.
properties.name: OPEN — what belongs in the design graph and what belongs in an agent's memory, and why the rule that already says so keeps losing
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill on Anthony's /brainstorm, 2026-09-19, after a session that wrote fifteen traps into a machine-local memory file while the graph held the rule forbidding exactly that. Recorded as one question rather than two because he asked for the boundary to be settled once, and the delivery mechanism is an option within it rather than a separate subject. Kept separate from dec:idea-does-the-agent-keep-a-notepad-in-the-graph-for-the-next-agent, which asks whether an agent would READ notes left for it; this asks where a lesson BELONGS and why the existing rule does not bind.
